# Current optimization union

Current delivery is the [normal PC test package](../dev/artifacts/ShaderLOD-PC-1.21.1-NeoForge.zip), **Minecraft 1.21.1 NeoForge only**, all nine pinned families. The [readiness matrix](evaluation/pc-implementation-handoff-20261017.md) and three current inventories reconcile all 549 family/control cells. Applicable existing ports, independent controls, tuning and native recovery are implemented and checked for the stated scope. [PC instructions](PC_TESTING.md) cover the next RTX 5080 phase. Source declarations, actual rendering, quality and target-hardware speed remain separate. Historical owner proposals below do not override this handoff.

Working source inventory for the user-authorized
[union goal](goals/optimization-union-and-measurement.md). This is an implementation
artifact, not a competing task ledger. Parent finalizes IDs as owners inspect
actual source. Each meaningful independently controllable change gets its own
ID; primary and secondary consumers may require separate switches.

The live Java registry now has **61 canonical optimization IDs**. The source map
uses those keys; three old CPU names are aliases rather than separate measured
changes. Every family has a current disposition for each ID in the linked readiness inventories.
Older owner proposals below retain their historical provenance; a recorded ID alone is not a port.

Initial concepts found in maintained recipes and implementation classes:

| Provisional concept | Working source to reuse |
| --- | --- |
| Primary cloud density/detail rejection | BSL, Unbound/Reimagined, Bliss, Sildur, Solas, AstraLex, Photon current recipes |
| Secondary cloud lighting/ambient density rejection | Photon optical-depth call join |
| Native-count cloud opacity saturation exit | MakeUp Overworld and End |
| Cloud/volumetric sample budget with native interval/weighting | Sildur/Bliss/shared uniform budget and current family ports |
| Near volumetric-light work reduction | Complementary family current volume recipes |
| Valid-hit reflection refinement budget | Six family recipes and shared refinement helper |
| Aurora sample budget | BSL and Solas current recipes |
| Paired-depth AO sample budget | AstraLex deferred recipe |
| Native-AA-compatible pixel/render scale budget | Photon live-pixel recipe/common helper |
| Projected parallax/POM budget | Complementary projected-POM implementation; selected/optional status to establish |
| Cached quad fill, copied submissions, command compaction and associated caches | Family *quad eligibility/routes and pinned loader implementations |
| Existing geometry, effect and shadow traversal/culling optimizations | Shared main controllers/policies/mixins; exact consumers to establish |

This list is provisional and must be exhaustive against executable current
source, optional routes and selectors. A diagnostic ablation is not automatically
an optimization. Closed experiment results remain preserved; they do not
substitute for current code inventory or prove a new port profitable.

Per-feature shader switches will use individual integer uniforms under existing
bridge/global-enable/native-quality guards, avoiding unsupported GLSL bitmask
assumptions. Exact names/IDs are owned by the shared infrastructure owner and
will be frozen before final per-family integration. Owners may propose finer
components and identify previously missed optimizations with source evidence.

## Earlier integration history

Initial independent source ports are integrated for all nine families, with subsequent
Photon spatial, Bliss whole-frame, and Unbound/Reimagined/Sildur/Astra source
ports integrated. This is partial coverage of the union,
not completion of all 61 changes on every family. Resource-dependent AO, spatial,
shadow-field and history producers, their reload controls, and remaining CPU
consumers still require concrete joins. Missing producers remain pending.

Real frame, render-thread CPU, process CPU and GPU elapsed timing has been
exercised on MakeUp / NeoForge 1.21.1, including an individual OFF/ON/RETURN
comparison and cancellation/restoration. That demonstrates the measurement
backend; it establishes no speed benefit, final artifact identity, GUI behavior
or other loader/version coverage. See current STATUS for receipts and next work.


Latest direct source additions include certified reflected-density rejection in
both Complementary families, protected far shadow sampling, Astra's next-event
rough-reflection refinement, and Sildur's unused liquid AO call elision. Current
Unbound/Reimagined CPU vertex contracts are rebound with authentic full-source
proof; Sildur already passes. Astra's original/generated source certificates,
transformation input producers and ten rendering consumers are integrated.
Independent review found and repaired a draw-identity refusal bug. Actual Astra
rendering remains unverified and its native Mac hardware blocker is retained.

Normal source/setup hooks and bounded module identity have executed in the real
MakeUp client. The format directive repair reached the compiled graph; 282 AO
producer/return/consumer observations qualified. BSL subsequently recorded 1,702
qualified half-AO producer/return/consumer observations and skipped native
recovery. Both exercised individual Off and original Quality restoration. These
are functional rendering results, not quality or speed acceptance.

The index-size scalar cache now has source adapters for both 1.21.1 loaders,
alongside the existing two 1.21.11 adapters. Actual native fixtures preserve
masked-face counts and signed narrowing. Six newer targets already maintain the
maximum during emission and read its field; their bytecode documents the native
equivalent. Live activation of the new adapters and per-change cost remain
unverified. Solas and Unbound AO-depth receivers are integrated after independent
review and repairs of the shader qualifier connection and sampler proof. They
check the current owned program, depth texture, sampler and source at the native
draw, preserving implicit native sampling when unqualified. All ten current
normal production builds package the receivers, exact resources and registrations.
Actual positive GL qualification, avoided reads, quality and cost remain pending.

Solas now has source and input-admission joins for original and generated packs
on all ten targets, including the required NeoForge 26.2 binding correction.
Astra and Solas also recognize the exact Fabric 1.21.1 release input producer;
Loom's named producer and the release producer have separate pinned byte hashes.
All ten current production packages contain these changes. Package checks do
not establish actual Mixin application or rendering.

Astra's AO depth reuse retains every native 8/24 texture query and caches the
pure linear-depth calculation when its raw input repeats. Its nearest-cell
texture cache was refused because the proposed coordinate-error bound was
unproved. Reconstruction savings and texture-read savings remain distinct.
MakeUp's shadow-footprint producer and Sildur's minimum-field joins are still
under integration; Sildur's intended filtered-shadow lookup avoidance remains
unfinished.

Sildur now also reuses the homogeneous denominator and reconstructed depth when
successive AO samples have exactly equal raw depth. Every native texture query
and each sample's fresh screen/TAA coordinates remain. The reviewed source and
certificates reached a normal build; actual GPU savings remain unverified.

Bliss's reviewed reflection metric port caches the invariant reciprocal only
after the first failed traversal visit. Native traversal, additions, first-hit
behavior and texture queries remain unchanged. Its source is synchronized into
the shared adapter resources and catalog. The effect is optional: both native
specular reflections and screen-space reflections must be enabled. The exact
runtime profile and current vertex/source joins now reach normal Fabric 1.21.11
and NeoForge 26.2 packages. Live reflection consumption and the optional profile
on other loaders remain unverified.

Unbound's independent zero-emission shortcut now skips its scalar emission
multiplication only at exact zero. Native material and lighting work stays intact;
its source, certificates and exact vertex dependency row are integrated. Sildur's
independent reflection projection control now omits only the unused terminal
depth-range calculation after the last unsuccessful visit. It retains all native
depth queries and hit tests. Both passed independent source and public recovery
checks; updated normal builds, rendering and speed remain separate acceptance.

Current all-ten packages now contain those Unbound and Sildur ports plus Bliss's
independent zero-emission port. Bliss omits its exposure/power/target arithmetic
only at positive-zero emission inside the reviewed finite/normal domain; it
retains the native final mix and falls through to literal native work otherwise.
The earlier broad exposure domain was refused and remains negative evidence.

Fabric 1.21.11's six additional full release API variants reached the actual
normal JAR and passed its real selectors against pinned runtime provider bytes.
All nine port modules now copy Photon API data from the shared resource; stale
local API copies had previously disagreed with the shared reader's hash. Exact
resource/reader pairs are verified in all ten current JARs. These delivery checks
do not prove live Mixin application, GL qualification, quality or frame cost.

BSL's receiver reduction now has actual normal sampler-setup callbacks for all
eight modern targets, preserving the two legacy callbacks. The source guard
admits only the six pinned Minecraft/Iris pairs, including Fabric 1.21.1's
distinct Iris version. Its AO source pin, mandatory binding certificate and exact
vertex closure were updated together. All ten normal packages contain the
selected callbacks and current resources; actual sampler qualification and
rendered reduction remain unverified.

Sildur's native POM recurrence does permit a certified height-prefix port. The
old recurrence-based exception is withdrawn. Its conditional source now omits
only reads that cannot terminate the ray under a strict returned-height bound,
retaining repeated coordinate advances and first-hit behavior. It explicitly
rejects nonfinite gradients. The real atlas/sampler/epoch producer and operative
nMap2 profile are still pending, so packaged source is not an active completed
optimization.

Sildur's exact nMap2 source profile now passes its main and NeoForge 26.2
source/binding gates while the existing CPU eligibility remains restricted.
Solas has a normal NeoForge 1.21.1 atlas/sampler/static-sprite/epoch producer and
exact operative advanced-material/POM profile. Its original default AO source
pin and CPU closure were preserved. All ten current JARs package the changed
source, but the other nine Solas producer adapters remain pending.

MakeUp's candle arithmetic port and narrow vertex proof are integrated. Native
lightmap bias prevents the ordinary default path from reaching exact zero;
held-light cutoff is the concrete optional opportunity. Photon now has normal
history target/sampler/draw hooks: qualified invalid reprojection can omit six
unused reads, while valid reprojection retains six. Observation failures clear
history before retry; native draw failures retain their original exception.
Actual normal ProgramSet registration and GL consumption remain runtime checks.
These source and package deliveries establish no frame-time improvement.

A fresh NeoForge 1.21.1 client compiled and rendered the current MakeUp candle
source, accepted individual zero-emission On/Off while holding the other 60
requests fixed, and returned to its original shader under Quality without
fallback. Held-light cutoff activity, avoided arithmetic and visual/performance
effects were not measured. A separate Photon probe failed its unchanged original,
generated adapter and original-return deferred4 pass at the Mac driver's 16
fragment-sampler limit: the pass requires 17. This is a local native-original
runtime boundary, not positive evidence for Photon history consumption.

Sildur now has its first normal NeoForge 1.21.1 atlas producer. It checks the
current source/profile, linked terrain functions, static winning sprites,
actual normal image/sampler and lifecycle epoch before publishing descriptors
and permissions. The normal JAR contains its selected hooks and pinned data.
Actual GL capture/publication and the other nine producer adapters remain
pending; the native default still leaves POM off.

Current production-consumer inspection found four unresolved renderer ports.
Early alpha rejection, depth priming and merged terrain still have real
implementations only in private development experiments. Their canonical normal
switches do not yet invoke those algorithms. Terrain-radius reduction has a real
normal consumer only on NeoForge 1.21.1; the other nine source selections omit
its controller and hook. These remain implementation gaps across applicable
families, rather than completed shared optimizations or feature exceptions.
The current owners are porting early alpha into MakeUp, depth priming into
Unbound, and the terrain controller into the missing targets. Merged terrain
still needs normal family-specific source, draw and restoration joins.

At October 14 11:07 UTC, Solas and Sildur each have three additional integrated
normal producers: Fabric 1.21.1 and both loaders on 1.21.11. All three changed
target builds passed, and immutable JAR checks verified current source resources,
producer classes and registrations. Solas's modern sampler predicates now match
the native sampler's -1000/+1000 LOD defaults while retaining texture levels
0 through 4. Each family still lacks six producer adapters and positive live GL
capture/consumption evidence. See the [build receipt](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/normal-build-solas-sildur-r13/artifact-receipt.json).

BSL's first normal NeoForge 1.21.1 POM producer is integrated and packaged.
Independent review also repaired native PBR selection and complete stored-base
profile replay on NeoForge 26.2; public Apply/Off/Quality checks passed without
granting the separate CPU or receiver permissions. Both changed normal builds
passed. Nine other producer adapters and live rendering remain pending. See the
[BSL receipt](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/normal-build-bsl-prefix-r14/artifact-receipt.json).

The nine-target terrain controller candidate is not adopted: review found that
a generation transition could reuse stale coverage confirmation and warmup,
and an early confirmation could transfer to a different scene. Its owner is
repairing revocation and confirmation. It is not counted as complete.

Fabric 26.2's binding-cache port is now integrated for all nine shader families,
after independent review repaired its BSL native PBR clause. Its normal build
and immutable JAR checks pass, including the nine source certificates, selected
native pins and Mixin registration. Cache hits retain full byte stamps each
draw and avoid repeated ZIP/member/profile replay; switching the cache off
retains fresh certification and the mandatory native correction. Eight other
cache routes and loaded rendering/cost acceptance remain pending. See the
[Fabric cache build receipt](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/normal-build-binding-fabric262-r15/artifact-receipt.json).

MakeUp's first normal early-alpha producer is now integrated for NeoForge 1.21.1.
It prepares native alpha rules before shader pruning, owns the actual cutout
program, qualifies current samplers at the native draw and revokes permission
afterward. Independent source/API/recovery review passed. All ten normal builds
package its current shared shader source and source guards; the other nine
targets exclude the legacy producer and still require their own API ports.
See the [early-alpha build receipt](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/normal-build-all10-earlyalpha-r16/artifact-receipt.json).

Reimagined's conditional POM prefix source is also integrated after independent
binary32 recurrence review. Its next-step threshold and forced final read
preserve native final height, coordinates and hit index. Its normal producer
and complete operative RP2/RP3 profile bindings were subsequently integrated
for NeoForge 1.21.1. Independent review repaired an RP2 stored-state/RP3 live
profile mismatch in the NeoForge 26.2 source certificate. All ten current normal
JARs contain the six exact RP2/RP3 profile/function resources; the first normal
producer is registered. Actual linked shader/atlas capture and read avoidance,
plus nine producer APIs, remain pending. See the [current build receipt](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/normal-build-all10-reimagined-r21/artifact-receipt.json).

Review refused MakeUp's merged-terrain candidate because its derived program
does not inherit early-alpha or shadow ownership. Turning merged draws on would
silently disable those peers, invalidating an independent comparison. The owner
is repairing explicit derived-program admission; geometry/API checks alone do
not close that defect. Measurements must also account for effective terrain
coverage being revoked by generation changes: unchanged switch values alone do
not prove unchanged effective rendering work. These are remaining integration
requirements, not positive performance results.

The repaired terrain-distance consumer is integrated across all ten targets,
including typed optional DH adapters, normal tick/Options hooks and explicit
scene confirmation commands. Generation changes revoke old coverage and warmup;
confirmation binds the current inspected scene. All ten builds and JAR checks
passed. Loaded DH coverage, rendering and cost remain unverified. See the
[terrain build receipt](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/normal-build-all10-terrain-r17/artifact-receipt.json).

MakeUp's merged-terrain producer is integrated for NeoForge 1.21.1 after the
derived-program ownership repair. It shares the actual native fragment and
uses its own qualified vertex/TBO path; early-alpha and shadow permissions are
independent. Nine remaining targets exclude the legacy implementation. All ten
builds passed. A real launch then exposed duplicate normal/private Mixin names;
the normal configs and region helper now have distinct names, preserving the
private experiment. The fresh real client rendered the current generated pack,
accepted early-alpha On, merged On, merged Off and early-alpha Off with the
other 59 requests fixed, and returned to the original under Quality without
fallback. The exact client was stopped. These are rendering/control/restoration
results, not proof of private alpha permission, merged TBO submission, quality
or speed. See the [functional receipt](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/makeup/alpha-merged-functional-r20/runtime-evidence.json).

NeoForge 26.1.2 now exposes the independent binding-cache control on its real
terrain source-admission consumer. The old code already memoized identity and
options; the new On path adds full byte/resource/flag guards, while Off forces
fresh validation. No original-baseline speed gain is inferred. Its actual normal
JAR contains the fingerprint helper and caller.

Unbound's depth-priming candidate remains unadopted. Review found a leftover
private property gate, missing normal admission installation and cleanup that
missed some thrown errors. Its owner is repairing those actual entry points;
pure control plans and compilation did not prove a working normal route.

Those Unbound normal activation and cleanup defects were repaired and reviewed.
The first NeoForge 1.21.1 implementation is now integrated, including the
independent 406-option compile control, native invariant vertex/coverage path
and restored native color draw. All ten normal packages build with current
Unbound source and exactly one shared options resource; the other nine depth
producer APIs remain pending. A real client rendered the original and generated
pack, accepted Depth On, then crashed with `depth restore GLerror=1280` in the
normal restoration verifier. Its exact session stopped and prior controls were
restored. Runtime activation/recovery therefore remains failed and under repair;
no positive depth work, quality or speed result is claimed. See the [failed runtime receipt](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/unbound/depth-functional-r25/runtime-evidence.json).

The failed depth run was repaired with the core GL4.1 active-unit sampler-binding
query; the strict restoration/error checks remain intact. A fresh real normal
client now completed compile option 0→1→0 with the other 60 requests fixed.
Solid and cutout terrain each submitted their coverage program, verified native
draw state restoration, and returned to the original shader under Quality
without fallback. The exact client exited and all flags were restored. This
establishes normal FML/Mixin activation and GL behavior within this scene, not
visual quality or a speed gain. See the [successful runtime receipt](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/unbound/depth-functional-r27/runtime-evidence.json).

MakeUp early alpha is also integrated on Fabric 1.21.1 with its actual Fabric
loader/provider pins and module-local runtime; normal build/JAR checks passed.
Eight further early-alpha targets and Fabric draw permission remain pending.
Solas's fifth normal POM producer, NeoForge 26.1.2, is integrated after its
both-gradient finite-domain repair. Its combined build is underway; actual
capture/consumption and five further producer APIs remain pending. All ten
current JARs now package this source, and the five intended Solas producer
targets contain their normal hooks and resources.

A focused Bliss source review withdrew the blanket cloud-opacity exception.
The normal cloud marcher already exits below extinction 1e-5, but enabling
`RAYMARCH_CLOUDS_WITH_FOG` excludes the fog loop's native exit. That optional
cloud contribution is now an assigned source port; independent fog radiance and
atmosphere alpha must be preserved. Finite arithmetic, exact-zero reachability,
derivatives and native option/profile joins are not yet proven. Existing Bliss
volume and reflection budget consumers remain source implementations, with
their resampling quality limitations retained. See the [source review](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/bliss/source-frontier-r1/REPORT.md).

BSL early-alpha is now integrated for normal NeoForge1.21.1. It preserves
native GREATER0.1, atlas alpha and the existing receiver derivatives; eligible
rejected cutout fragments can skip downstream lighting/shadows. Owned nonmipped
shadow samplers qualify surviving explicit-LOD reads; unsupported paths remain
native. All ten normal builds/JAR checks passed with the new BSL recipe and
BSL-only vertex closure; only the declared first target has its runtime. Nine
producer APIs, actual draw permission, quality and cost remain pending. The next
Fabric1.21.1 port uses its actual locked Iris1.8.8 tuple. See the
[adoption receipt](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/root-adoption/bsl-early-alpha-r1/receipt.json)
and [artifact receipt](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/normal-build-bsl-alpha-r33/artifact-receipt.json).

Solas now has six normal POM producers after the Fabric26.1.2 port; MakeUp
merged terrain has two after Fabric1.21.1. Actual builds/package checks passed,
while their new live GL/quality/cost boundaries remain unverified. Independent
review refused the first Fabric file-control join: reload LinkageError could
leave new flags or core settings persisted. Its narrow canonical recovery repair
is active; file receipt acceptance alone will not stand in for restoration.

BSL's second early-alpha producer is integrated for Fabric1.21.1 on its locked
Iris1.8.8 tuple. Independent review verified its11 local files, exact named and
release API profiles and unchanged source/recipe/vertex rows. The actual remapJAR
contains the local Fabric runtime and sole normal config; build inputs did not
drift. Eight producer targets and live draw qualification remain pending. See the
[Fabric artifact receipt](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/normal-build-bsl-alpha-fabric1211-r34/artifact-receipt.json).

The comparison constructor has a separate reproduced native Error recovery gap:
a controlled callback through the actual comparison class persists its Off flag,
throws LinkageError and fails to restore the original snapshot. Canonical flag/core
Apply repairs and comparison/scene lease repairs have separate owners. A fresh
Fabric world has been prepared for ordinary control/restoration; no timing or
comparison launch is inferred from that preparation.

Unbound's missing POM empty-height prefix source and first normal NeoForge1.21.1
producer are integrated. Review verified the native Reimagined-identical march,
exact next continuing-threshold law, complete398/406 RP2/RP3 replay, atlas/sampler
and lifecycle controls, and depth-pin coexistence. All ten builds/JAR checks
passed; only the first declared target has the normal runtime supplier. Nine
APIs, positive current GPU qualification, actual skipped reads and quality/cost
remain pending. Prior9f archive recognition is retained while current7d guards
remain strict. See the [adoption](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/root-adoption/unbound-prefix-normal-r1/receipt.json)
and [artifact receipt](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/normal-build-unbound-prefix-pair-r36/artifact-receipt.json).

The three comparison recovery consumers are also integrated and packaged. Fresh
independent checks restore the original reproduced failed flag while preserving
the same Error; failed flags/source/scene/query ownership stays explicit. Actual
private-server freeze/future recovery and GPU query cleanup still need runtime
validation. The clocks and export backend were preserved.

The first real Fabric ordinary-control run failed before toggles: BSL and MakeUp
early-alpha registered competing redirects on the same uniform builder call.
Iris disabled shader rendering when BSL's required injection was skipped. The
exact client was stopped and release verified; its profile/receipts/log remain
preserved. The two-loader BSL repair changes registration to a distinct native
builtin call, preserving default0, MakeUp's final builder hook and strict
injection requirements. It is under independent review; static builds/selector
checks did not prove combined activation. See the
[actual failure diagnosis](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/renderer-joins/fabric1211-functional-r1/failure-diagnosis.json).

After the composable BSL registration repair, the fresh real Fabric client
completed current MakeUp Performance, alpha On, merged On/Off, alpha Off,
Quality original-return and original Off. Every request was accepted; full61
flags, native100 options and initial core state were restored. Actual running
JVM/DLI inputs show named normal/dev classes/resources, not literal remapJAR
consumption. The exact client exited with zero clients and free runtime lock.
Private alpha/TBO admission, avoided work, quality and speed are unverified. See
the [successful Fabric control receipt](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/renderer-joins/fabric1211-functional-r2/runtime-evidence.json).

Unbound's second normal POM prefix producer is integrated for Fabric1.21.1.
The exact Iris1.8.8 source permit retains the NF1.8.12 path; all six emitted
shader stages and398/406 RP2/RP3 profiles match the accepted NF implementation.
All ten builds and actual JAR checks passed, with the normal supplier installed
only on the two intended targets. Eight APIs and liveGL/read avoidance/quality
and cost remain pending. See the
[Fabric adoption](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/root-adoption/unbound-prefix-fabric1211-r1/receipt.json)
and [artifact checks](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/normal-build-unbound-prefix-fabric-r38/artifact-receipt.json).

Reimagined's first normal early-alpha producer is integrated on NeoForge1.21.1.
The port handles actual IPBR material alpha resampling after the initial native
discard, executing after native AO/bias derivatives and before shadow probes.
Independent source/profile/API/public recovery review passed; all ten builds
and actual JAR source/row checks passed, with the runtime installed only on the
first target. Nine APIs, actual permission/work avoidance, quality and cost
remain pending. Old current source recognition is retained. See the
[adoption](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/root-adoption/reimagined-early-alpha-r1/receipt.json)
and [artifact checks](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/normal-build-reimagined-alpha-r40/artifact-receipt.json).

The first framebuffer-mismatch timing attempt has now been recovered through a
distinct real normal cancel/Quality/Off operation. The original failed logs and
preimages remain; source/core/options/flags returned to their actual original
state. A fresh comparison used actual settled matching native Window/FBO
dimensions and completed240 samples in each Off/On/Return phase for all five
clocks, with native GPU query provenance and checked raw/metadata denominators.
Private simulation, source/options/full61 flags/core and original selection
were restored before exact stop. On was slower and Off/Return drift was large;
no causal gain or winner is accepted. See the
[actual export validation](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/renderer-joins/fabric1211-measurement-r2/measurement-validation.json).

Solas and AstraLex first normal NeoForge1.21.1 early-alpha producers are now
integrated. Solas preserves material/POM/generated-normal/voxel work before the
new gate; Astra preserves material resampling, PBR, rain, lava and caustics. Both
use actual owned sampler laws for post-rejection queries. Independent native
source/API/public restoration reviews and all ten actual build/JAR checks pass.
Only the two declared first targets contain these runtimes; nine APIs each,
positive current permissions, quality and cost remain pending. Source histories
and other family rows are retained. See the
[combined artifact receipt](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/normal-build-solas-astra-alpha-r47/artifact-receipt.json).

The early-alpha validation cache is integrated into seven NeoForge 1.21.1 and
three Fabric 1.21.1 normal rendering paths. It retains full raw source/dependency
fingerprinting and per-draw sampler, owner and permission checks, while
independently switching unchanged semantic-validation replay. Independent review
and 315 authentic public checks pass; all ten normal builds package the helper
and exact resources. Only those ten existing consumers use the cache; native
hits, work, cost and consumer adapters for the other eight targets remain
pending. See the [artifact receipt](../dev/logs/optimization-union-20261014/normal-build-source-cache-r48/artifact-receipt.json).

The timing CLI now requires exporter completion and matching raw counts, means
and GPU provenance before reporting a complete bracket. Actual complete and
failed exports were checked. Completion of an export does not establish stable
workloads, matching source identities or a causal speed benefit.

Photon and Unbound first normal NeoForge1.21.1 early-alpha ports are integrated.
Photon preserves strict native alpha<0.1 after final POM, skipping two optional
material textureGrad reads; its default already rejects at the earliest point.
Its generated vertex closure is unchanged, and allten builds/JAR checks pass.
Unbound handles native material alpha resampling, rejects after derivatives and
before four paired shadow positions, and preserves both depth0/1 graphs. Its
source/API/public review passes; the integrated build is next. All nine families
now have a first early-alpha source/normal route; broader APIs and positive
native work, quality and performance remain pending.

Parent review caught a source no-op in the initial Sildur Fabric candidate:
Java/public checks passed but the shader guard admitted only Iris10812 rather
than Fabric's10808. That candidate was not adopted. The corrected port must emit
the positive consumer under actual Fabric preprocessing; negative evidence is
retained. Current STATUS owns the corrected port and build sequence.

Sildur and Bliss second normal early-alpha producers are integrated for Fabric
1.21.1. Corrected Sildur source explicitly admits Iris10808 as well as10812;
actual positive shader emission, original Off output and10812 behavior pass.
Bliss source is unchanged and actual10808 whole-program emission passes. All ten
current r50 builds and JAR checks pass: nine NF1211 families and five Fabric1211
families have early-alpha routes; seven NF and five Fabric routes use the
source-validation cache. Other eight API targets lack these normal routes.
Fresh Unbound RP1/RP2/RP3 depth0/1 public source, source-certificate, CPU refusal
and Off/Quality checks pass. Native permissions, avoided work, quality/DH/PBR
and cost remain pending. Unbound, Solas and Astra Fabric ports are active.

All nine families now have early-alpha and source-validation-cache implementations
on both NeoForge and Fabric for Minecraft1.21.1. Unbound retains both depth
profiles. Photon uses an explicit fingerprint for its different maintained
manifest, including actual original-member and helper bytes, while preserving
full raw hashes and its optional material profile. Its default already rejects
early. Independent cache review passed74 cases per loader against current root
pins; Unbound passed33 fresh current-resource cases. Source guards and native
per-draw ownership/sampler/permission checks remain distinct.

All ten current builds pass. Actual JAR inspection found missing Photon Fabric
config/profile resources; two explicit imports repaired that gap. Fabric was

## What caused the gap between less shader work and no FPS gain

Two observed CPU mechanisms were substantial: repeated source validation on
active render paths, and validation/resource observation on Photon's inactive
history path. Compile/link receipts move immutable input verification away from
draws while retaining live ownership, option, sampler and restoration checks.
Photon's inactive repair supplies direct before/after runtime evidence; removing
source calls on AO establishes CPU work removal without establishing an AO win.

Depth replay and half-resolution AO also add work: geometry submissions,
producer targets, binding checks and reconstruction. Current MakeUp/Unbound
depth clocks show increased render CPU and total-frame time. Half-AO permission
counts show valid producer execution, not how many pixels avoid native AO:
fallback/partial-confidence paths can retain the original kernel as well as new
producer/reconstruction costs. Exact per-component allocation remains unproved.

GPU reductions are conditional. Far shadow, visible clouds, water and full-
confidence AO each have different eligible coverage. Native compilation may
already remove some dead work; explicit/implicit sampling and dynamic loops
can affect code generation. Those are hypotheses where not isolated by an A/B
experiment. Source tap counts are not issued hardware-instruction counts.
